questions.stemHtml: A 35-year-old male presents with complaints of weakness, fatigue, and frequent urination for the past few weeks. His blood pressure is 150/100 mmHg, and he has hypokalemia. His serum aldosterone level is found to be elevated. Which of the following is the most likely cause of his symptoms?
questions.solution: Correct Option A - Primary aldosteronism: The clinical scenario described in the question is consistent with the features of hyperaldosteronism, a disorder that results in excess production of aldosterone from the adrenal gland. The most likely cause of hyperaldosteronism in this patient is primary aldosteronism, which is also known as Conn's syndrome. This condition results in increased aldosterone production, leading to hypertension, hypokalemia, and metabolic alkalosis. questions.stemHtml: A 45-year-old female presents to the endocrinology clinic complaining of increased irritability, sensitivity to heat, weight loss, and vibrations. Laboratory tests show an increase in free T4 and a decrease in TSH. Which mechanisms are most likely responsible for the observed changes in this patient's thyroid gland physiology?

questions.solution: Correct Option A - Autoantibodies against thyroid-stimulating hormone receptors: The patient's clinical features of increased irritability, sensitivity to heat, weight loss, and vibrations suggest hyperthyroidism , which is characterised by increased thyroid hormone production. Autoantibodies against thyroid-stimulating hormone (TSH ) receptors are key in developing Graves' disease, the most common cause of hyperthyroidism. These autoantibodies, known as thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulins (TSI), bind to and activate the TSH receptors on thyroid follicular cells, mimicking the action of TSH. As a result, the thyroid gland produces and releases excessive amounts of thyroid hormones (T3 and T4), leading to the symptoms associated with hyperthyroidism. The binding of TSI to TSH receptors triggers a cascade of events, including increased iodine uptake, thyroid hormone synthesis, and thyroid gland growth. The elevated levels of thyroid hormones in the bloodstream then exert negative feedback on the hypothalamus and pituitary gland, suppressing the release of thyrotropin-releasing hormone (TRH) and TSH. This feedback loop results in the decreased TSH levels typically observed in patients with Graves' disease. The clinical manifestations of hyperthyroidism due to Graves' disease include heat intolerance, increased irritability, weight loss, palpitations , and fatigue. Additionally, patients may develop Graves' ophthalmopathy , characterised by exophthalmos (protrusion of the eyeballs), periorbital oedema, and diplopia (double vision). Incorrect Options: Option B - Increased production of thyroxine-binding globulin: Increased thyroxine-binding globulin (TBG) production can lead to elevated total T4 levels but would not affect free T4 levels or cause the symptoms described in the scenario. TBG binds to thyroid hormones, reducing their free (biologically active) concentrations. Changes in TBG levels usually have minimal effect on thyroid function. Option C - Ingestion of excessive amounts of dietary iodine: While excessive iodine intake can cause thyroid dysfunction, it typically results in hypothyroidism (reduced thyroid function) rather than the hyperthyroidism observed in this case. The Wolff-Chaikoff effect describes a transient decrease in thyroid hormone synthesis due to high iodine intake, leading to decreased thyroid function. Option D - Dysfunction of the parathyroid glands: Dysfunction of the parathyroid glands can result in abnormal calcium metabolism but does not directly affect thyroid gland physiology. The parathyroid glands produce parathyroid hormone (PTH), which regulates calcium homeostasis, and are not involved in producing or regulating thyroid hormones. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following is true concerning the estimation of nutritional needs in a critically ill patient?

options.label: A
options.text: Albumin and prealbumin are the best measures of nutritional status in critically ill patients

options.label: B
options.text: Lipid infusions are associated with an increased rate of infections in critically ill patients

options.label: C
options.text: Healthy patients have a daily protein requirement of 1.8 g/kg/day actual body weight

options.label: D
options.text: The absence of bowel sounds is a contraindication to enteral feeding

questions.answerText: Lipid infusions are associated with an increased rate of infections in critically ill patients
questions.solution: Correct Option B - Lipid infusions are associated with an increased rate of infections in critically ill patients: Although a short period of nutritional deprivation may be tolerated, physiologic function and nutritional status are affected by significant deprivation over 1-2 weeks. Factors that influence the need for nutritional supplementation include pre-illness status and severity and duration of metabolic stress. In critically ill patients, nutritional support should be initiated relatively as early as 24-48 hours after admission, as it may improve outcomes. If oral intake cannot maintain adequate nutritional intake, enteral or intravenous routes should be considered. Enteral nutrition is preferable when it is tolerated. Patients who will require 7 days or more of nutrition support should be considered for parenteral nutrition. Incorrect Options: Option A - Albumin and prealbumin are the best measures of nutritional status in critically ill patients: Albumin and prealbumin are acute phase reactants and may be falsely elevated in critically ill patients. Option C - Healthy patients have a daily protein requirement of 1.8 g/kg/day actual body weight : The protein requirement for a healthy patient is 0.8 g/kg/day actual body weight. Option D - The absence of bowel sounds is a contraindication to enteral feeding : The only contraindication to enteral feeding is high bowel obstruction. Lack of bowel sounds or lack of flatus are not contraindications to enteral feeding. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.stem: A 65-year-old man presents to physician with rectal bleeding for the past several months. His hemoglobin is 9.8 g/dL. He undergoes a colonoscopy that reveals a large, friable mass in the ascending colon and another smaller mass in the transverse colon. Biopsies of both masses confirm the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. An abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan reveals multiple hypodense liver lesions consistent with metastatic spread. Treatment with chemotherapy combined with cetuximab is considered. Which of the following genetic mutations should be tested prior to initiating therapy with cetuximab ?
questions.stemHtml:
A 65-year-old man presents to physician with rectal bleeding for the past several months. His hemoglobin is 9.8 g/dL. He undergoes a colonoscopy that reveals a large, friable mass in the ascending colon and another smaller mass in the transverse colon. Biopsies of both masses confirm the diagnosis of adenocarcinoma. An abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan reveals multiple hypodense liver lesions consistent with metastatic spread. Treatment with chemotherapy combined with cetuximab is considered.
Which of the following genetic mutations should be tested prior to initiating therapy with cetuximab ?
questions.solution: Correct Option D - KRAS: Cetuximab is a monoclonal antibody that inhibits epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR). It improves survival in metastatic colon cancer. The presence of KRAS-activating mutations predicts a poor response to cetuximab therapy. Therefore, cetuximab is restricted to patients with wild-type (nonmutated) KRAS. Incorrect Options: Option A - APC: APC (Adenomatous Polyposis Coli) mutations are associated with familial adenomatous polyposis (FAP), a condition characterized by the development of numerous colorectal polyps. It is not directly relevant to the decision of using cetuximab in this case. Option B - MSH2: MSH2 is a gene associated with hereditary nonpolyposis colorectal cancer (HNPCC), also known as Lynch syndrome. It is involved in DNA mismatch repair. While Lynch syndrome increases the risk of colorectal cancer, it is not specifically linked to the response to cetuximab. Option C - SMAD4: SMAD4 is a tumor suppressor gene involved in the TGF-β signaling pathway. Mutations in SMAD4 can be associated with certain cancer types, including pancreatic cancer. However, SMAD4 mutations are not typically assessed before initiating cetuximab therapy. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.stem: A 42-year-old female patient comes to your OPD to discuss further management of GERD. She was initially tried on H2-blocker therapy and had an initial response that was then lost. She was subsequently started on PPIs twice daily and has had inadequate symptom improvement. Recent VOGD demonstrates persistent esophagitis but no Barrett’s esophagus or mass lesion. pH studies confirm the presence of GERD. She is frustrated by her remaining symptoms, which have begun to affect her ability to exercise and sleep and her ability to swallow various foods safely. She has also been experiencing worsening regurgitation lately, which was confirmed by a manometry study last month. She asks whether surgery will lead to symptom improvement. Which of the following statements is true regarding anti-reflux surgery in this patient?

options.label: A

options.label: B
options.text: Anti-reflux surgery has been shown to improve symptoms in patients with regurgitation.

questions.answerText: Anti-reflux surgery has been shown to improve symptoms in patients with regurgitation.
questions.solution: Correct Option B - Anti-reflux surgery has been shown to improve symptoms in patients with regurgitation: Multiple studies have shown that while anti-reflux surgery does help with symptoms in certain patients, it does not alter an individual’s risk for esophageal cancer. Fundoplication should be reserved for patients with proven regurgitation using esophageal manometry studies. Endoscopic anti-reflux procedures including radiofrequency augmentation of the lower esophageal sphincter and endoscopic suturing of the sphincter have not been proven to result in long-term symptom control. Studies have shown that at 3 years after the procedures, patients continued to need medical therapy or a fundoplication procedure. Anti-reflux surgery is contraindicated in patients with metaplasia or dysplasia since it can affect treatment options in case of progression to cancer. Finally, anti-reflux surgery is associated with worsening of dysphagia in some patients; thus, there is no guarantee that her dysphagia will resolve. It is also associated with gas-bloat syndrome and diarrhea. Incorrect Options : Option A - Anti-reflux surgery will eliminate her risk of esophageal cancer: Anti-reflux surgery can reduce the risk of esophageal cancer by effectively controlling acid reflux and reducing inflammation in the esophagus. However, it does not entirely eliminate the risk of esophageal cancer, especially in patients with a long history of GERD and esophagitis. Option C - Endoluminal antireflux procedures are as effective as anti-reflux surgery without the associated complications of surgery: Endoluminal antireflux procedures, such as endoscopic suturing or radiofrequency ablation, are minimally invasive techniques that aim to improve reflux symptoms. While they may be effective in selected cases, they are generally not considered as effective as traditional anti-reflux surgery (fundoplication) for patients with more severe GERD symptoms or those with anatomical abnormalities like hiatal hernia. Option D - Since she has no evidence of metaplasia or dysplasia on EGD, she is not a candidate for antireflux surgery at this time: The presence or absence of metaplasia or dysplasia (Barrett's esophagus) on EGD (Esophagogastroduodenoscopy) is an important factor in determining the risk of esophageal cancer and the need for surveillance. However, it is not the sole factor in deciding whether a patient is a candidate for antireflux surgery. The decision to proceed with surgery should be based on the severity of symptoms, response to medical therapy, and other factors assessed by the treating physician. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.solution: Correct Option C - Epinephrine injection to the bleeding diverticulum with hemostatic clipping as needed for stigmata: Diverticular bleeding originates about 50% of the time from the right half of the colon, either at or proximal to the splenic flexure. questions.stem: Which of the following parasitic infections is usually associated with occult blood in stool?
questions.stemHtml: Which of the following parasitic infections is usually associated with occult blood in stool?
questions.solution: Correct Option D- Strongyloides: TRUE: Occult blood in stool is associated with hookworm or Strongyloides infection. Strongyloides stercoralis enters the human host when skin contacts the larvae through infected soil usually contaminated with feces. The parasite can live for up to 5 years in humans, eventually burrowing into the mucosa of the duodenum as adults. Eggs produced by the adult female pass in the feces. Eosinophilia points to a parasite infection. The adult worm migrates to the small bowel and can cause duodenitis, leading to epigastric pain that is aggravated by food ingestion. Patients complain of diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and anorexia. Pulmonary manifestations can include wheezing, dyspnea, and hemoptysis. Patients may complain of a dry cough, and chronic infection may result in recurrent pulmonary symptoms that are suggestive of bacterial pneumonia. Diagnosis is usually made by detection of characteristic larvae in stool or by serology. Incorrect Options: Option A-Coccidiosis: FALSE: Coccidiosis is associated with chronic tropical diarrhea. Option B- Giardia: FALSE: Giardia is associated with a malabsorption syndrome. Option C-Isospora belli: FALSE: Isospora belli is a parasite that causes chronic tropical diarrhea. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.answerText: Definitive therapy is hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and removal of extrapelvic lesions that are symptomatic
questions.solution: Correct Option D - Definitive therapy is hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy and removal of extrapelvic lesions that are symptomatic: A trial of medical therapy is usually the initial line of treatment in patients with endometriosis, but surgical treatment is definitive. Since rectovaginal and bowel endometriosis coexist with other diseases, definitive treatment is hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy with removal of rectovaginal lesions. Incorrect Options: Option A - Rectal endoscopic ultrasound is the first-line study for evaluation of rectovaginal endometriosis: Transvaginal ultrasound is the first study used for evaluation of rectovaginal endometriosis because rectal endoscopic ultrasound is associated with more discomfort and the need for sedation. Option B - A double-contrast barium enema is the initial recommended imaging test for suspected endometriosis: Double-contrast barium enema may reveal information about partial bowel obstruction, but the information is not specific to endometriosis, so it is not useful for evaluation or initial diagnosis. Option C - Sigmoidoscopy and colonoscopy are the most useful studies for the identification of bowel endometriosis: Sigmoidoscopy and colonoscopy have limited utility since endometrial lesions do not usually penetrate the mucosa. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.stemHtml: Which of the following biliary cysts involves both the intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary tree?
questions.solution: Correct Option D - Type IV biliary cyst: Type IVA biliary cysts affect both the intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary tree. Type IVB is associated with only extrahepatic lesions. Again, both are associated with an increased risk for cholangiocarcinoma. Thus, it is recommended that they are excised to minimize this risk. Incorrect Options: Option A - Type I biliary cyst: Type I biliary cyst is a simple cystic dilatation of the extrahepatic bile duct (common bile duct). It does not involve the intrahepatic biliary tree. Option B - Type II biliary cyst: Type II biliary cyst, also known as choledochal cyst with diverticulum, is a diverticulum arising from the common bile duct. It is limited to the extrahepatic biliary tree. Option C - Type III biliary cyst: Type III biliary cyst, also known as choledochocele, is a dilation of the intraduodenal portion of the common bile duct. It involves the terminal portion of the extrahepatic biliary tree but not the intrahepatic ducts. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.stemHtml: A patient with autoimmune hepatitis is undergoing liver transplantation for decompensated cirrhosis. Which of the following is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The matching of HLA alleles between donor and recipient has been demonstrated to reduce the risk of recurrence of AIH to <5%.

options.label: B
options.text: The median time for development of recurrent AIH is 5 years after liver transplantation

options.label: C
options.text: Corticosteroids are ineffective in the treatment of AIH recurrence in the allograft

options.label: D
options.text: Compared to patients with other etiologies of liver disease, patients with AIH have a higher frequency of acute and chronic rejection

questions.answerText: Compared to patients with other etiologies of liver disease, patients with AIH have a higher frequency of acute and chronic rejection
questions.solution: Correct Option D - Compared to patients with other etiologies of liver disease, patients with AIH have a higher frequency of acute and chronic rejection: Compared to patients with other etiologies of liver disease, patients with AIH have a higher frequency of acute and chronic rejection, which may be the result of immune hyperactivity. After recurrent AIH in the allograft is identified, patients will require re-introduction of corticosteroids if they have been withdrawn, in addition to optimized immunosuppressant therapy. Incorrect Options: Option A - The matching of HLA alleles between donor and recipient has been demonstrated to reduce the risk of recurrence of AIH to <5%: The relationship between HLA matching and the development of recurrent AIH in the allograft is unclear. Option B - The median time for development of recurrent AIH is 5 years after liver transplantation: Recurrent AIH develops after a median 2-year period after transplant. Option C - Corticosteroids are ineffective in the treatment of AIH recurrence in the allograft: Corticosteroids should be reintroduced if they have been withdrawn, in addition to optimized immunosuppressive therapy. Azathioprine and prednisone are usually effective for the treatment of recurrent AIH. @Neet_pg_bot

After recurrent AIH in the allograft is identified, patients will require re-introduction of corticosteroids if they have been withdrawn, in addition to optimized immunosuppressant therapy.

Incorrect Options:

Option A - The matching of HLA alleles between donor and recipient has been demonstrated to reduce the risk of recurrence of AIH to <5%: The relationship between HLA matching and the development of recurrent AIH in the allograft is unclear.

It demonstrates multiple focal dilations of both the intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary tree. Which of the following statements regarding this patient’s lesion is true?

options.label: B
options.text: Anatomical and/or functional obstructions likely contribute to the pathogenesis of these lesions.

options.label: D
options.text: This patient’s lesion places her at an increased risk for cholangiocarcinoma.

questions.answerText: This patient’s lesion places her at an increased risk for cholangiocarcinoma.
questions.solution: Correct Option D - This patient’s lesion places her at an increased risk for cholangiocarcinoma: This patient has a type IV A biliary cyst. It is the only type of biliary cyst that presents with both intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary dilation. Type IVB only has extrahepatic biliary cysts. It is associated with an increased risk of cholangiocarcinoma. Incorrect Options: Option A - Estrogen and progesterone are thought to play a role in the pathogenesis of this patient's lesion: The focal dilations of both the intrahepatic and extrahepatic biliary tree described in the patient are characteristic of a condition known as Caroli disease. Caroli disease is a congenital disorder that involves non-obstructive saccular or fusiform dilations of the intrahepatic bile ducts. The role of estrogen and progesterone is not linked to the pathogenesis of Caroli disease. Option B - Anatomical and/or functional obstructions likely contribute to the pathogenesis of these lesions: Caroli disease is characterized by non-obstructive biliary dilations, meaning that there is no significant mechanical obstruction contributing to the development of the dilations. Option C - This patient's condition is hereditary: Caroli disease can be hereditary in some cases, but it can also occur sporadically without a family history. It is important to evaluate the patient's family history to determine if there is a hereditary component in this specific case. @Neet_pg_bot

questions.stem: A 73-year-old male undergoes surveillance MRI of a mass in side branch in the uncinate process discovered incidentally 2 years earlier on CT. At that time, FNAC revealed benign cytology. The patient had a CEA level of 840. Today, the lesion is 3.5 cm with a 5 mm mural nodule. Which of the following is indicated in the management of this patient?
questions.stemHtml: A 73-year-old male undergoes surveillance MRI of a mass in side branch in the uncinate process discovered incidentally 2 years earlier on CT. At that time, FNAC revealed benign cytology. The patient had a CEA level of 840. Today, the lesion is 3.5 cm with a 5 mm mural nodule. Which of the following is indicated in the management of this patient?
questions.solution: Correct Option D - Surgical resection: This presentation suggests intraductal papillary mucinous neoplasm (IPMN) of the pancreas, a grossly visible neoplasm that is potentially malignant and composed of mucin-producing cells, as evidenced by the patient’s CEA (>800). Resection is indicated for tumors with features suggestive of malignancy. Features that suggest malignancy include dilation of the main pancreatic duct to >7 mm, cystic lesions >30 mm with an irregular thick septum in branch duct lesions, and mural nodules that are >10 mm. Incorrect Options: Option A - Repeat MRI in 6 months: The lesion has progressed, and watchful waiting is not an appropriate strategy. Option B - Repeat EUS-FNA: This is unlikely to add information or change management. Approximately 50-60% of fluid samples are acellular or not diagnostic. Option C - Octreotide scan: Octreotide scanning has no utility in this case. @Neet_pg_bot
